source.author: verg
source.text: Intonuere poli, et crebris micat ignibus aether, praesentemque viris intentant omnia mortem.
source.text_original: Intonuere poli, et crebris micat ignibus aether, / praesentemque viris intentant omnia mortem.
source.text_english: The heavens thundered, and the ether flashed with repeated fires, and all things threatened the men with death, now close at hand.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quomodo igitur crebris micat ignibus aether; et in ictu oculi atque momento discurrunt fulgura et revertuntur, non amittentia matricem, et, ut ita dicam, fontem ignis atque materiam: ita et haec animalia cum inoffenso pergant pede, ad priora festinant.
reuse.text_original: Quomodo igitur crebris micat ignibus aether; et in ictu oculi atque momento discurrunt fulgura et revertuntur, non amittentia matricem, et, ut ita dicam, fontem ignis atque materiam: ita et haec animalia cum inoffenso pergant pede, ad priora festinant.
reuse.text_english: So then, just as the sky flashes with frequent fires, and in the blink of an eye and a moment the lightnings dart out and return, not losing their source, and, so to speak, the fountain and material of the fire: so also these living creatures, as they proceed with unhindered foot, hasten onward to what is before them.
